item.title: Deptford Green Secondary School reach EFL Girls' Cup National Finals
item.description: Deptford Green Secondary School, who are representing Millwall at the EFL Girls Cup, have reached the nationals of the competition. After winning the local tournament between schools at The Lions Centre in December, Deptford Green progressed on to the regional stages. The next stage took place at Charlton Athletic’s Sparrow Lane, where the side came second. item.title: Under 21s held to late draw at Swansea
item.description: Millwall's Under 21s were held to a 1-1 draw at Swansea City in the Professional Development League on Tuesday afternoon. Elias Mansor opened the scoring for The Lions, but just as it looked as though Kevin Nugent's side would claim an away victory, Swansea equalised a minute from time through Sam Parker. item.title: Over £6,000 raised on Jimmy's Day!
item.description: A record-breaking total of £6,052.29 was raised for the Mizen Foundation last weekend. Raised through bucket collections and more, the sum represents the largest fundraising in Jimmy's Day history. On the field, The Lions kept their unbeaten run on 'Jimmy's Day' going with a 4-0 demolition of Charlton Athletic in the Sky Bet Championship. item.title: Barry Bannan's first words as a Millwall player
item.description: Barry Bannan is a Millwall player. The midfielder has signed for The Lions for an undisclosed fee from Sheffield Wednesday, penning an 18-month contract at The Den. During his media duties, the Scot sat down with Millwall TV+ to discuss his arrival in South London, his hopes for the remainder of 2025/26 and beyond and more - including touching on his departure from Hillsborough. Click play on the video below to hear from Barry.

item.title: Millwall confirm Barry Bannan signing
item.description: Millwall Football Club is delighted to announce the signing of Barry Bannan from Sheffield Wednesday. The midfielder joins The Lions for an undisclosed fee and pens an 18-month contract in SE16. Bannan, 36, moves south after a decade at Hillsborough, where he became an Owls legend after making over 450 appearances across the Sky Bet Championship and League One.
